title: ENDEX: 17:00, Queues at WATCH and Night Shift Handed Over

fields.resolution: ENDEX. EXERCISE, EXERCISE, EXERCISE. It is 17:00 on Thursday. Calls and texts are at WATCH on the platform, and the wall board on GPCN-OPS-01 is catching up. The call share under NOC-26-03118 and the state backup center's text share are both still running under a written hand-off to the night shift, and they will be released only after an hour at OK. This concludes the exercise.
finalState: GPCN staff are working the 19 routine follow-up callbacks, oldest first.
Every counselor who carried the surge has had a break. Those who asked have been offered time with Dr. Anneliese Park, and the group check-in is booked within 48 hours.
The final status went to the state 988 coordinator. The partner message went to school districts and local officials.
The vigil wording went to NEMA and the disaster behavioral health team. Each of these was sent after a safe messaging review.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Please put down your phones and headsets. Remember that everything today was fictional, and support is still available after this session. Dr. Anneliese Park is here, and you can step out at any time. Before we start the hot wash, we will go around the room. Each person names one thing that helped them stay steady today.
fields.hotWashMethod: Steady round first, so each person names one thing that helped them stay steady. Then we walk the timeline. For each decision point, we name what we saw, when we acted and what we would change.
hotWashQuestions: The wall board ran two 15-minute intervals behind the platform. When did each of you stop trusting the board, and what should trigger a level change in future?
The text queue went over its WATCH threshold at 13:20, and backup was asked for at 14:14. How did that timing compare with the 60-minute rule, and what would get the request out sooner?
At 15:30 we chose whether to move texts to the secondary messaging route. What information did we have, what did we not have, and who should own that decision?
The call-in list showed 38 people as available, but 11 could not be reached. What has to change before the next quarterly check?
The Level 2 post, the state status and the media reply all ran behind the rumor. Which statement should have gone first, and who could have released it?
fields.facilitatorNote: Content is complete. Open with the steady round before any review, and watch for anyone who goes quiet. Make sure Dr. Park stays in the room through the hot wash. Have the Communications Lead record the 14-day review of every statement released today, and have the Workforce Coordinator take an action on the call-in list. Collect the surge logs and evaluator sheets before people leave.
